Explanation: The core value unit is an available seat on a trip that is already going in the passenger's direction. BlaBlaCar makes that spare capacity searchable and bookable.
BlaBlaCar operates the travel marketplace that connects passengers with carpool drivers and also distributes bus and train offers.
BlaBlaCar has to find planned trips with spare seats and connect them with travellers going the same way.
More useful routes and successful bookings make the marketplace more attractive to both travellers and drivers.
Long-distance demand is spread across many routes and departure times, so a passenger may not always find a suitable trip.
BlaBlaCar makes trip offers searchable, manages booking and payment flows, and connects both sides before the journey.
Transaction Flows: ← Consumer · Search / Book — The passenger asks BlaBlaCar to find a suitable trip and books through the platform. | → Provider · Match — BlaBlaCar connects a passenger request with a driver's planned route and spare seat. | ← Partner · Bus / Rail — Professional operators provide scheduled routes, fares and seat inventory to BlaBlaCar's marketplace. | → Partner · Bookings — BlaBlaCar distributes operator offers and sends completed bookings into the professional transport network.

Explanation: BlaBlaCar sets identity, review and booking rules and limits carpool contributions so drivers do not use the service for profit.
Travellers and drivers reach the marketplace through BlaBlaCar's apps, website, search and local market activity.
The platform matches routes, manages bookings and payments, supports members and operates trust and safety systems.
Important resources include traveller demand, driver supply, route data, reviews, payment systems and the BlaBlaCar brand.
Travellers use BlaBlaCar to find affordable long-distance trips by car, bus or train.
Passengers want a convenient way to travel between cities, including places that may have limited direct public transport.
Carpooling can lower travel costs and add direct connections to places that are harder to reach by scheduled transport.
A suitable driver may not be available, plans can change, and meeting points or departure times may be less predictable than scheduled services.
Passengers search for a suitable trip, reserve a seat and pay through the platform where booking is enabled.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Search / Book — The passenger asks BlaBlaCar to find a suitable trip and books through the platform. | ← Provider · Shared Ride — The driver provides the passenger with a seat on the trip the driver was already planning to make. | → Provider · Cost Share — The passenger contributes toward the driver's trip costs; the driver is not meant to make a profit from carpooling.

Explanation: A trip is useful only when the route, date, departure time and available seat match the passenger's needs.
Passengers search, compare and book carpool, bus and train options through the BlaBlaCar app and website.
Passengers search for a route, choose an offer, book a seat, meet the driver or operator and complete the journey.
Passengers bring destination demand, timing preferences, payment and reviews to the marketplace.
Carpool drivers are ordinary people already making a trip who offer spare seats to passengers travelling the same way.
Drivers want to reduce the cost of a trip they already intend to make by sharing fuel and other travel expenses.
Filling empty seats lets drivers recover part of their trip costs without turning the journey into a professional transport service.
Drivers may face meeting-point detours, passenger cancellations, delays or uncertainty about whether seats will be filled.
Drivers publish a planned trip and available seats; passengers contribute toward the costs of that journey.
Transaction Flows: ← Owner · Match — BlaBlaCar connects a passenger request with a driver's planned route and spare seat. | → Consumer · Shared Ride — The driver provides the passenger with a seat on the trip the driver was already planning to make. | ← Consumer · Cost Share — The passenger contributes toward the driver's trip costs; the driver is not meant to make a profit from carpooling.

Explanation: BlaBlaCar's terms require carpooling to remain non-commercial: drivers cannot request more than their actual trip costs or use the platform to make a profit.
Drivers post routes, manage bookings and communicate with passengers through BlaBlaCar's platform.
Drivers publish their planned route, accept passengers, coordinate pickup and complete the journey.
Drivers contribute the vehicle, a trip they already planned, spare seats and their time on that journey.
Professional bus and rail operators add scheduled transport offers to the same traveller marketplace.
Transport operators add scheduled alternatives where carpool supply may be unavailable or where travellers prefer a professional service.
Operators can reach BlaBlaCar's travel demand and sell additional seats through another distribution channel.
Scheduled operators need enough passengers to fill capacity and make routes economically attractive.
Operators make schedules, fares and seat inventory available for search and purchase through BlaBlaCar.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Bus / Rail — Professional operators provide scheduled routes, fares and seat inventory to BlaBlaCar's marketplace. | ← Owner · Bookings — BlaBlaCar distributes operator offers and sends completed bookings into the professional transport network.

Explanation: An operator must serve relevant routes and meet the commercial and technical requirements for distribution on the platform.
BlaBlaCar connects professional transport inventory through digital distribution and operator systems.
Operators manage scheduled services, capacity, pricing and the physical transport operation.
Operators contribute scheduled routes, vehicles, seat inventory, timetables and operating capacity.
